newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: NKorea tells aid agencies children dying - UN.
newsitem.headline: NKorea tells aid agencies children dying - UN.

text.p: North Korea has told international aid agencies in Pyongyang that a total of 134 children have died of malnutrition so far in the country's growing food crisis, a United Nations official said on Tuesday.

Hans Olsen of the U.N. Children's Fund UNICEF said the figure -- believed to be the first on mortality from food shortages provided by the secretive communist state -- was given by a health ministry official at a meeting on Monday.

Olsen told a news briefing that it was not clear from the official's remarks over what period the deaths had occurred. North Korea has suffered two disastrous harvests in a row after heavy rains and floods in 1995 and 1996.
On Monday, the United Nations Department of Humanitarian Affairs (DHA) launched an appeal in New York for $126.2 million to stave off an imminent famine in North Korea.
"The situation can be described as a humanitarian disaster in the making," DHA chief Yasushi Akashi told a news conference.

At Tuesday's Geneva briefing, a spokeswoman for the U.N.'s World Food Programme, also heavily involved in getting supplies into North Korea, said the agency was coming to the conclusion that "famine is virtually inevitable in the coming months".
